extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of 19th-century slave narratives / autobiographical prose
extracted.subtask_description: Autobiographical slave-narrative prose that recounts episodes of violence, escape, and daily life in antebellum America, using vivid scene-setting, dialogue, and moral reflection. Useful as an exemplar of evocative narrative technique and rhetoric in 19th-century non-fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: vivid_sensory_detail_and_setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete sensory details (sight, sound, touch) to evoke place and danger: e.g., "the moon arose..., long, pendent moss..."; "the swamp was resonant with the quacking of innumerable ducks"; descriptions of moccasins, alligators, mud, torn clothes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground scenes in specific sensory imagery to make setting tangible and emotionally effective. Give concrete details (animals, plants, sounds, physical sensations) rather than abstract statements about 'danger' or 'desolation.' Example: the repeated details of water depth, mud, snakes, and alligators create sustained peril. Anti-pattern: vague or generic descriptors that fail to convey atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: dramatic_action_and_immediate_conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage scenes of physical danger and high stakes with immediate, present-tense momentum: the hatchet attack, the struggle over the broad-axe, and the flight through the swamp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show conflict through rapid beats of action, short sentences or clauses at key moments, and specific physical moves (grips, kicks, seizing arms). Use these sequences to maintain narrative tension and propel the reader. Avoid diffusing urgency with long, abstract digressions in the middle of the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: characterization_through_dialogue_and_dialect
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal character by distinctive speech and colloquial phrasing (e.g., Peter Tanner's mocking salutations and the slaves' dialectal lines like "I _know'd_ dey would'nt cotch him").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use idiosyncratic phrasing, punctuation, and word choice to make characters distinct and believable. Let dialogue reveal status, temperament, and relationships. Care: use dialect purposefully to convey authenticity and power relations without reducing characters to caricature or unreadable phonetic spellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: moral_reflection_and_interiority
rubrics_metrics.description: Interleave action with moral and internal reflection (e.g., narrator's contemplation of death, appeals to God, lament for family): "I sighed for liberty... I could only gaze wistfully towards the North."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance outward events with inward response to deepen reader empathy and articulate the narrator's ethical perspective. Use rhetorical questions and direct appeal to the reader or to God to heighten the moral frame. Avoid interrupting tension with reflections that don't connect to the scene's stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: use_of_biblical_allusion_and_religious_framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ scriptural references and religious language as moral commentary and rhetorical reinforcement (e.g., comparisons to Daniel and Jonah; the planter reading Luke and citing 'many _stripes_').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategically use familiar religious allusions to resonate with readers' moral horizons and to contrast professed piety with abusive behavior. Example: religious quotations are used both to justify punishment and to condemn cruelty. Anti-pattern: gratuitous allusion that doesn't illuminate character or theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: specific_proper_nouns_and_place_names_for_authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor narrative in named people and places (Tibeats, Ford, Peter Tanner, Bayou Boeuf, Great Pacoudrie Swamp, Cheneyville) to increase verisimilitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete names and local details to lend documentary weight and situate events historically and geographically. Proper nouns act as credibility signals in autobiographical writing. Avoid over-generalizing or anonymizing if authenticity is the goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: juxtaposition_of_cruelty_and_kindness
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast brutal episodes (whippings, hatchet attack, chase by hounds) with acts of kindness (Master Ford's protection, food and rest) to shape reader sympathy and moral judgement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use opposing demonstrations of behavior to make moral evaluations vivid: show both abuse and small mercies to portray complexity and to highlight injustice. Anti-pattern: flattening all characters into uniformly evil or uniformly good without nuanced evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: structural_summaries_as_chapter_headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use chapter headings that summarize or preview content in compact phrases (e.g., the all-caps headings listing events such as 'RETURN TO TIBEATS--IMPOSSIBILITY OF PLEASING HIM--HE ATTACKS ME WITH A HATCHET').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ informative chapter headings to orient readers and create anticipatory momentum. Headings can function as a table of contents in miniature and set tonal expectations. Avoid misleading or overly cryptic headings that confuse rather than guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: show_don't_tell_through_concrete_action
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer showing the stakes through concrete action (the narrator's physical struggle, flight, and bodily sensations) rather than abstract moralizing alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let readers infer emotional states and moral meaning from what characters do and endure. Use action to exemplify character and theme; follow with brief reflective lines as needed. Anti-pattern: long expository passages that summarize events after the fact without dramatizing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: precise_physical_danger_details_to_heighten_realism
rubrics_metrics.description: List specific threats and bodily consequences (moccasin snakes 'their bite more fatal than the rattlesnake's', alligators, loss of a shoe, thorns, scratches) to increase credibility and reader concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate concrete hazards and physical suffering to make danger believable and to justify characters' decisions. These particulars also serve to document the material conditions of flight and survival. Avoid vague statement of 'dangers' without particulars.
